outline.description: Presents the core problem of controlling large text-to-image diffusion models and motivates orthogonal finetuning (OFT) as a principled approach to preserve pretrained generative semantics while adapting to downstream tasks.
subtopics: Limits of text-only control in diffusion models
Downstream tasks: subject-driven generation and controllable generation
Desiderata for finetuning: efficiency and preservation of generalization
Shortcomings of conventional finetuning and adapter-style approaches
High-level idea: preserving pairwise neuron geometry on the hypersphere

outline.chapter_title: Background: Diffusion Models and Finetuning Landscape
outline.description: Reviews text-to-image diffusion models and existing finetuning strategies, setting the context for OFT.
subtopics: Text-to-image diffusion models: pixel-space vs latent-space (GLIDE, Imagen, Stable Diffusion, DALL·E 2)
Text and vision-language backbones (CLIP, VQ-GAN, text encoders)
Standard finetuning with small learning rates
Adapter-based finetuning (Adapters, LoRA): mechanisms and trade-offs
ControlNet and T2I-Adapter for controllable generation
Subject-driven generation (DreamBooth) and its challenges

outline.description: Introduces hyperspherical similarity and hyperspherical energy as structural measures of neuron relationships that correlate with semantic preservation.
subtopics: Neuron direction vs magnitude: why angles matter
Cosine similarity and angular representations in deep learning
Definition of hyperspherical energy (HE) for a layer
HE as a proxy for pairwise neuron uniformity and semantic structure
Invariance of pairwise angular relationships under orthogonal transforms
Intuition from Fourier magnitude/phase separation

outline.description: Builds intuition and empirical justification for applying layer-shared orthogonal transformations to pretrained weights during finetuning.
subtopics: Rotations/reflections as the simplest global direction-only updates
Preserving HE to retain pretrained semantics
Trade-off: controlling degrees of freedom to prevent collapse
Toy evidence: angle-only information reconstructs semantics in autoencoders
Failure without orthogonality: instability and collapse case study

outline.chapter_title: OFT: Core Formulation and Layer-Wise Application
outline.description: Formalizes Orthogonal Finetuning and explains how it integrates into neural layers and transformer attention within diffusion models.
subtopics: Objective: minimize HE difference; solution via shared orthogonal matrices
Forward pass: W = R W0 with R orthogonal; identity initialization
Interpretation: change of neuron coordinate system; preserving pairwise angles
Applying OFT to different layers: fully connected, attention weights, convolutions
No inference overhead: folding R into W0 post-training

outline.description: Details practical parameterizations of orthogonal matrices to make OFT scalable and parameter-efficient.
subtopics: Challenges of differentiable orthogonalization (Gram–Schmidt costs)
Cayley transform: R = (I + Q)(I − Q)^{-1}, Q skew-symmetric
Determinant constraint and practical implications
Block-diagonal orthogonal matrices: structure and intuition
Parameter complexity: full vs r-block diagonal; optional block sharing
Comparative parameter counts with LoRA on concrete sizes

outline.chapter_title: Constrained and Re-Scaled Variants: COFT and Re-Scaled OFT
outline.description: Introduces two variants that improve stability and flexibility: COFT adds a radius constraint around identity; re-scaled OFT learns per-neuron magnitudes without changing HE.
subtopics: COFT: constraint ||R − I|| ≤ ε for controlled deviation
Implementing COFT with Cayley parameters via Neumann approximation and projection on Q
Effect of ε on flexibility vs preservation; empirical stability gains
Re-scaled OFT: W = R W0 D with diagonal D > 0; preserves HE while adding magnitude freedom
When to use each variant in practice

outline.description: Positions OFT relative to LoRA and other methods; analyzes why OFT converges fast and preserves semantics.
subtopics: Additive low-rank (LoRA) vs multiplicative full-rank constrained (OFT)
Rewriting OFT as W0 + (R − I)W0: implicit low-rank when (R − I) is low-rank
Two routes to parameter efficiency: low-rank vs block-sparse orthogonality
Optimization on smooth hypersphere manifolds: convergence intuition
Why minimizing HE is inappropriate for finetuning
Flexibility-regularity spectrum: standard finetuning, LoRA, OFT, COFT

outline.description: Explains how OFT/COFT integrate into the DreamBooth framework to preserve identity while following prompts, with metrics and results.
subtopics: Task setup: few-shot subject images + text prompts; preserving identity and prompt fidelity
Training protocol alignment with DreamBooth; layers finetuned with OFT/COFT
Evaluation metrics: DINO/CLIP-I (subject fidelity), CLIP-T (prompt fidelity), LPIPS diversity
Convergence and stability comparisons with DreamBooth and LoRA
Quantitative outcomes: fidelity/diversity improvements
Qualitative analyses: identity preservation and prompt adherence; robustness to longer training

outline.description: Covers integrating control signals (edges, segmentation, landmarks) and introduces a control consistency metric; compares to ControlNet, T2I-Adapter, and LoRA.
subtopics: Tasks and datasets: C2I (COCO), S2I (ADE20K), L2F (CelebA-HQ)
Training setup: finetuning SD v1.5; parameter counts vs adapters
Control consistency metrics: IoU/F1 (edges), mIoU/acc (segmentation), landmark L2 (faces)
Convergence speed and stability: epoch-wise curves and qualitative progression
Quantitative results: stronger control and quality with fewer parameters
Qualitative comparisons: structure adherence, fidelity, and diversity

outline.description: Provides actionable guidance for implementing OFT/COFT in diffusion pipelines with stable training and effective hyperparameters.
subtopics: Where to apply OFT: attention projections in U-Net/transformer blocks; optional conv layers
Initialization and parameterization: identity R via zero Q; Cayley and block structure choices
Selecting number of blocks r and sharing strategy
COFT hyperparameters: choosing ε and projecting Q
Optimizers, learning rates, and iteration budgets
Integrating with DreamBooth losses and control-conditioning pipelines
Exporting folded weights to avoid inference overhead

outline.description: Summarizes broader implications, theoretical and practical insights, and outlines future research directions opened by OFT.
subtopics: Architecture-agnostic nature: transformers and convolutions (depth-wise view)
Compositionality potential: chaining orthogonal matrices across tasks
Scalability: differentiable matrix inverse bottlenecks and faster parameterizations
Bias–flexibility trade-offs in block-diagonal designs
Human evaluation considerations and additional control modalities
Open questions: improved parameter efficiency, theory of semantic preservation via HE, multi-task orthogonal composition
